_meta.title: Terminology appendix — Uncomfortable Situations (back-of-book Index, Option-C hybrid filtering)
_meta.filtering_rule: Option C (hybrid): INCLUDE every concept or italicized work-title entry regardless of page-count; INCLUDE every author/interlocutor entry with ≥2 page references; EXCLUDE author entries that occur only at a single page or only in a note (bibliographic crumbs).

lemmas.definition: Pre-personal, pre-conceptual bodily intensity treated by Massumi as autonomous from emotion; in this volume contested as a useful theoretical division.
The interdisciplinary field organized around the affect/emotion distinction (Massumi, Berlant, Sedgwick, Ngai).
Gibson's term for action-possibilities offered by an environment to an organism; Gross extends it to rhetorical and literary environments.
Gibson's ecological-perception framework — the basis of Ch. 3's reading of hostile gothic environments.
School of Black-studies theory (Moten, Wilderson, Sexton) holding that Black social life is not lived within the world's modern-system codes.
Feminist queer phenomenologist whose Queer Phenomenology (2006) underwrites the volume's analyses of comfort, orientation, and whiteness.

lemmas.lemma: Anatomy and Philosophy of Expression as Connected with the Fine Arts, The
lemmas.definition: Charles Bell's 1844 anatomical treatise (with Laocoön plate) framing pre-Darwinian expressivism.
James Chandler's 2013 study of the sentimental mode in literature and cinema.
Classical rhetorician whose Rhetoric Book II provides the volume's running analytic for emotion-as-judgment in situation.
Denis Dutton's 2009 evolutionary-aesthetics manifesto cited as exemplar of evocriticism.
Le Brun-derived passion linked classically to admiration and fear; Gross's main category for analyzing Austen's mixed-feelings scenes.
Merleau-Pontian intentional bond between body and world; in Ch. 2 the analytic of Equiano's relationship to master and to freedom.
Primary author of Ch. 4; her Sense and Sensibility is read as a critique of utilitarian/Benthamite emotional calculus.
Affective neuroscientist whose constructed-emotion / situated-conceptualization program provides the volume's empirical-science scaffold.
Cognitive scientist (Emory) of grounded/situated conceptualization; co-author of the 2011 epigraph paper.
Paul Ekman's program of universal, hard-wired discrete emotions (anger, fear, disgust, sadness, joy, surprise, contempt); the volume's running critique-object.
Scottish anatomist whose Anatomy and Philosophy of Expression (1844) is Darwin's antecedent in physiognomic analysis.
Eighteenth-century moral-sentiments virtue whose Austenian critique runs through the Sense and Sensibility chapter.
Utilitarian philosopher whose hedonic calculus is the genealogical target of Ch. 4 and the scientific antecedent of Kahneman.
Affect theorist whose 'situation' analytic (Cruel Optimism 2011) Gross supplements with rhetorical exigence.
Rhetorician whose 1968 essay 'The Rhetorical Situation' defines exigence/audience/constraints, which Gross translates as basic discomfort.
Frantz Fanon's 1952 study of the phenomenology of colonized embodiment.

sub_entries: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
lemmas.definition: English Romantic poet whose Songs of Innocence and Experience supply Chandler/Goldsmith's sentimental-criticism corpus.
Rhetorical critic whose Rhetoric of Fiction (1961) is invoked on Austen's Emma.

lemmas.lemma: Bourgeois, The: Between History and Literature
lemmas.definition: Franco Moretti's 2013 study of bourgeois comfort and form in the nineteenth-century novel.
Literary Darwinist (On the Origin of Stories 2009) whose evocriticism Ch. 3 critiques.
fMRI imaging technologies adopted by emotion neuroscience; Gross's running methodological worry concerns reverse-inference.
The contemporary neuroscience of emotion (Damasio/LeDoux/Ekman) — the volume's primary scientific antagonist.
Rhetorician whose Philosophy of Literary Form and Permanence and Change supply the comfort/recalcitrance dialectic.
Critical theorist whose Psychic Life of Power (1997) on passionate attachments grounds Gross's reading of Equiano.

lemmas.lemma: Cambridge Handbook of Situated Cognition, The
lemmas.definition: Robbins & Aydede edited volume — Griffiths & Scarantino's 'Emotions in the Wild' contribution is the standing reference.
Penguin editor and Equiano biographer; key for the South-Carolina-birth controversy.
Literary Darwinist whose 'Human Life History and Gene-Culture Coevolution' (2011) is a primary text for Ch. 3.
Neuroimaging design (Ollinger/Shulman/Corbella 2001) addressing Kagan's surprise problem in event-related fMRI.
Cognitive literary critic of Thinking with Literature (2016) — interlocutor on literary affordances and praeteritio.
Philosopher of mind whose foreword to Clark's Supersizing the Mind (2008) is a standing reference on extended mind.
Literary historian whose Archaeology of Sympathy (2013) anchors the sentimental-mode framework.
Philosopher of cognition (Supersizing the Mind 2008) — extended-mind theorist.
The umbrella label for cognitive literary studies and literary Darwinism — Gross's persistent critical foil.
Information-processing paradigm whose computational assumptions Gross's situated approach contests.
Lakoff/Turner-style program of cognitive-linguistic analysis applied to literature.
The interdisciplinary mind-science field whose situated/embodied wing the volume embraces.
The volume's central organizing concept — bourgeois comfort as ideological scaffold whose discomfort generates rhetorical situation.

lemmas.lemma: Compassion: The Culture of Politics and Emotion
lemmas.definition: Berlant-edited 2004 anthology on compassionate-conservatism politics of emotion.
E. O. Wilson's program of unified humanities-and-sciences explanation; running antagonist in Ch. 3 and Epilogue.
Evolutionary psychologist (Adapted Mind, 1992); cofounder of EP program.
Cognitive literary critic (Shakespeare's Brain 2001) — interlocutor on CAL.
Martha Nussbaum's 2011 capability-approach treatise.
The legal-and-cultural-studies framework grounding Gross's analysis of racialized fear and master-slave attachment.
Lauren Berlant's 2011 book — the volume's signature affect-theory reference.
The 'New Historicist' / cultural-studies frame against which CAL positions itself.
Williams/Hall-tradition of left literary-cultural analysis.
Neuroscientist (Feeling of What Happens 1999) whose somatic-marker hypothesis is the volume's persistent foil.
Author of The Expression of the Emotions (1872) — primary text of Ch. 1; recovered as rhetorician of emotional situations rather than Ekmanian universalist.
Phillip Prodger's 2009 study of Darwin's use of photography in the Expression.
Literary critic and Equiano scholar; defends 'Olaudah Equiano, Written by Himself' (2006).
Historian of empathy/Holocaust trauma whose 'Erasures' (2014) anchors the Epilogue.
The volume's master concept — basic-discomfort = rhetorical exigence; the negative condition that produces rhetorical situation.
Ekman 'basic emotion'; Gross's analyses recurrently complicate its discrete-category status.
Franco Moretti's 2013 collection — Stanford Lit Lab quantitative method.
Elaine Scarry's 1999 book on perception and reading.
Phenomenologist and philosopher of AI whose embodied-cognition program is a primary ally.
Pioneer of Black studies; The Souls of Black Folks supplies the double-consciousness analytic for Ch. 2.
Nineteenth-century neurologist whose facial-electrical-stimulation photographs Darwin adapted in the Expression.
American psychologist (1932) — recovered as proto-situated-emotion theorist.
Author of The Art Instinct (2009); evolutionary-aesthetics popularizer.
Literary-criticism program oriented to environment; reframed here as rhetorical ecology of affordances.

lemmas.lemma: Ecological Approach to Visual Perception, The
lemmas.definition: James J. Gibson's 1979 magnum opus on affordances.
Deidre Shauna Lynch's 1998 study of novel-and-mind reading as bourgeois subjectivity.
Psychologist of universal facial expressions and developer of FACS; the volume's principal scientific antagonist.
The book's central object — recast from internal-mental-state to externalized, situated rhetorical phenomenon.
The post-Darwinian laboratory science of emotion (Ekman/LeDoux/Damasio); the volume's critical target.
The interdisciplinary humanities field of affect/feeling studies.
Lipps-derived term central to mirror-neuron and social-neuroscience programs; the Epilogue's primary critical object.
Hegel's Philosophy of Mind section invoked on extended-mind avant la lettre.
The Gibsonian/Lewinian concept of organism-context; the analytic framework of Ch. 3.
Black-Atlantic author of The Interesting Narrative (1789) — primary text of Ch. 2.
Brian Boyd's evolutionary-aesthetic criticism program; treated as ecologically remote by Gross.
Gottschall/Carroll edited literary-Darwinist anthology.
Cosmides/Tooby/Pinker program inferring cognitive adaptations to a Pleistocene environment of evolutionary adaptedness.
The orthodox-EP capital-letter brand whose disciplinary commitments Ch. 3 contests.
Bitzer's term for the imperfection-marked-by-urgency that calls a rhetorical situation into being.

lemmas.lemma: Expression of Emotions in Man and Animals, The
lemmas.definition: Darwin's 1872 treatise — the primary text of Ch. 1.
Clark-Chalmers thesis that cognition extends into tools and environment.
Ekman's facial-musculature coding scheme — the methodological foundation of basic-emotions science.
Anticolonial theorist whose phenomenology of Black embodiment Ch. 2 mobilizes.
Ekman 'basic emotion' whose neuroscientific operationalization the Epilogue critiques (esp. Phelps amygdala-race studies).
Colloquial English category Gross uses interchangeably with emotion when both terms apply.
In Equiano, simultaneously an economic transaction and an affective horizon — generative of the 'happy situation' rhetoric.
Author of Das Unbehagen in der Kultur — the German Unbehagen behind the volume's title 'Uncomfortable Situations.'
Black-studies critic; Black Imagination and the Middle Passage (1999) is cited on Equiano.
Koffka/Lewin school of figure-ground perception; affordance theory's nearest historical ancestor.
Ecological psychologist whose affordance theory anchors Ch. 3.
Author of Blake's Agitation (2013) — cited on Chandler-style sentiment criticism.
Author of The Rhetoric of Sensibility (2005); historical context for Ch. 4.
Walpole/Radcliffe/Lewis genre — the literary archive of hostile environments in Ch. 3.
Philosopher of science (Emotions in the Wild) — 'scaffolding' interlocutor; co-editor of Don't Give Up on Basic Emotions.
Philosopher of science whose TLS review (1998) of Damasio is repeatedly cited.
Author of Scenes of Subjection (1997) — anchors slavery-as-attribution analytic.
The Kahneman-Diener program of empirical happiness research.
Philosopher whose master-slave dialectic and Phenomenology of Spirit anchor Ch. 2's reading of Equiano.
Philosopher whose 1924 GA 18 Aristotle-rhetoric lectures are the volume's hidden philosophical hinge (Intro n.37).
Narrative theorist whose third-wave cognitive approach incorporates Umwelt research.
Empathy researcher (with Preston); Michigan dissertation work on personal representations.
CAL critic; 'Literary Universals' in the Zunshine handbook.
Steven Pinker's 1997 evolutionary-psychology synthesis.
Post-WWII framework that Bailkin and others read alongside the welfare-state emotion regime.
Wimsatt/Beardsley 1946 doctrine; Carretta's note on Equiano renders it relevant to Ch. 2.

lemmas.lemma: Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano, The
lemmas.definition: Equiano's 1789 autobiography — primary text of Ch. 2.
Zunshine-edited 2010 volume — the field-defining CAL anthology.
The volume's pejorative for the gut-reaction model of behavior critiqued via Kahneman.
Developmental psychologist (What Is Emotion? 2007) — the volume's preferred internal-to-science critic of Ekman.
Behavioral economist and Nobel laureate whose hedonic-psychology program structures Chs. 2 and 4.
Eighteenth-century philosopher whose Critique of Pure Reason is invoked on Equiano (via Gilroy).
Literary critic of Actions and Objects (2010); aesthetics-of-presence interlocutor.
Cognitive linguist; Metaphors We Live By; Women, Fire, and Dangerous Things.
The Hellenistic sculpture group whose pain-expression Darwin footnotes via Lessing.
Neuroscientist of fear/amygdala — alternative target alongside Damasio.
Gestalt social psychologist whose 'hopeless situation' and valence-of-environments analysis anchor Ch. 3.
Critical historian of science; her 'Turn to Affect' (2011) structures the volume's affect-theory engagement.
The Carroll/Boyd/Gottschall school applying Darwinian theory to literary explanation.
Raymond Williams's 1961 work — source of 'structure of feeling.'
The volume's recurrent test case for situated emotion analysis.
William Reddy's 2012 historical-emotion study of courtly love across Eurasia.
Author (with Engels) of the Feuerbach critique invoked in Ch. 2 on objects and social demands.
Affect theorist whose Parables for the Virtual (2002) defines the autonomy of affect.
Author of Bourgeois Virtues (2007) — Austen-as-Aristotelian-virtue interlocutor.
Phenomenologist whose Phenomenology of Perception (1945) is Ch. 2's second epigraph.
The Zunshinean Theory-of-Mind program applied to fiction; cross-reference: see Theory of Mind.
The Rizzolatti/Gallese program; treated critically in the Epilogue via Leys.
Schiller-derived concept central to Ch. 4 — Austen's analytic of emotional ambivalence as situational rather than psychological.
Candace Pert's 1997 popular-neuroscience book.
M. G. Lewis's 1796 gothic novel — sentence-form analyzed in Intro for negation effects.
Literary historian; Stanford Lit Lab — the bourgeois-paradox-of-comfort interlocutor.
Vivasvan Soni's 2010 book on the politics of modernity and happiness.
Gross's running umbrella term for novels as cognitive-rhetorical environments.
Laurence Horn's natural-history-of-negation framework; key to litotes-affordance argument in Introduction and Ch. 4.
Alan Richardson's 2010 book on Romantic-period cognitive science.
Varela's program of integrating first-person and third-person methods in consciousness studies.
The Epilogue's primary critical object — Gross and Preston's review of money-incentive, reverse-inference, and racialized-fear research.
Literary affect theorist; Ugly Feelings (2005) and Our Aesthetic Categories (2012).
Philosopher of perception whose Out of Our Heads (2009) and Varieties of Presence (2012) supply the contemporary situated-cognition baseline.
Lynch's Economy-of-Character thesis: novel-reading calibrates bourgeois interiority.
Philosopher whose neo-Stoic Upheavals of Thought and capability approach Ch. 3 contextualizes.
Iris Marion Young's 2005 phenomenology of feminine embodiment.
Schiller's 1795 treatise — Chandler's mixed-feelings source.
Brian Boyd's 2009 literary-Darwinist treatise.
Sianne Ngai's 2012 book on zany, cute, interesting.
Alva Noë's 2009 book — primary contemporary situated-cognition source.
Classical-Aristotelian rhetorical appeal; here recast as situated emotional attribution rather than internal feeling.
Evolutionary psychologist (How the Mind Works 1997); consilience-program strawman.
Philosopher whose Philebus is invoked on propositional-attitude-laden mixed feelings (via Frede).
